_note: All network indicators are stored DEFANGED ([.] for .). The site refangs in-browser only; feeds ship defanged. This keeps the repo safe for AV, mail gateways, and accidental clicks.

incidents.title: CVE-2026-21962 — Oracle HTTP Server/WebLogic Proxy flaw fuels 7-month China-linked campaign across 100+ countries
incidents.summary: A maximum-severity authentication bypass in the Oracle HTTP Server and WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-in lets an unauthenticated attacker with plain HTTP access compromise the instance and access or modify critical data. Oracle patched it in January 2026, but SOCRadar reported in July that a China-linked threat actor had been exploiting it since at least February against government and commercial networks in more than 100 countries — CISA added it to KEV Aug 24 with an Aug 27 federal deadline. Durable catch: any unpatched Oracle HTTP Server/WebLogic Proxy Plug-in reachable over HTTP has likely already been probed — this campaign ran undetected for seven months before public confirmation.
facts: CVSS 10.0 · UNAUTH ACCESS BYPASS
EXPLOITED 7+ MONTHS ACROSS 100+ COUNTRIES
CLOUDSEK HONEYPOT: 140,000+ ATTEMPTS FROM 21 COUNTRIES IN 12 DAYS
incidents.action: Patch Oracle HTTP Server and WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-in immediately if the January 2026 CPU has not been applied; assume compromise on any internet-facing instance that was unpatched between February and August 2026 and hunt for unauthorized data access or modification; restrict Proxy Plug-in endpoints from public HTTP access where patching is delayed; hunt for SNOWLIGHT downloader activity as the China-linked actor's follow-on payload.

iocs.context: Oracle HTTP Server/WebLogic Proxy Plug-in unauth access bypass, CVSS 10.0
Fix released 7 months before public confirmation of active exploitation
Follow-on payload delivered by the China-linked actor exploiting CVE-2026-21962

iocs.value: Unauthenticated HTTP requests to Oracle HTTP Server/WebLogic Proxy Plug-in endpoints from unexpected sources
iocs.context: China-linked exploitation pattern per SOCRadar; CloudSEK honeypot recorded 140,000+ attempts from 21 countries over 12 days

incidents.title: IRGC-linked CyberAv3ngers shut down a UK power plant for four days — first confirmed British power-generation standstill
incidents.summary: CyberAv3ngers, a hacking group affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps that specializes in breaching internet-exposed industrial PLCs, brought a small UK power station to a complete standstill for four days in July 2026 — the first time a hostile state has succeeded in halting British power generation outright. The Telegraph broke the story Aug 22; officials kept it low-key since the facility was small enough that the outage caused no disruption to the wider national grid, but the UK's National Cyber Security Centre wrote directly to energy companies with new guidance afterward. No PLC brand, malware family, or other technical indicator has been publicly disclosed for this specific intrusion — reporting rests on a single Telegraph source, and even SecurityWeek's coverage flags that gap directly. CyberAv3ngers' documented toolkit from prior campaigns (the IOCONTROL malware family, MQTT-over-TLS C2 on port 8883, targeting of Unitronics/Red Lion/Orpak equipment left on factory-default passwords) is background on how this actor typically operates, not a confirmed match to this incident. Durable catch: CyberAv3ngers' pattern is targeting small utilities and rural operators that expose PLCs directly to the public internet — that exposure, not the target's size, is what invites this actor.
facts: FIRST CONFIRMED UK POWER-PLANT STANDSTILL FROM CYBERATTACK
4-DAY OUTAGE · NO WIDER GRID IMPACT
NO TECHNICAL IOCs PUBLICLY DISCLOSED FOR THIS INTRUSION
incidents.action: Remove PLCs and other OT devices from direct internet exposure; place remote access behind VPN/gateway with MFA; small and rural utility operators should not assume their size makes them a low-priority target for CyberAv3ngers or similar IRGC-linked actors; review NCSC's post-incident guidance to energy operators.

iocs.context: Group responsible for the July 2026 UK power plant shutdown

iocs.value: Internet-exposed PLC management interfaces reachable without VPN/gateway restriction
iocs.context: Primary exposure this actor exploits across its victim set

incidents.title: CVE-2026-8452 — Citrix NetScaler pre-auth RCE exploited in the wild to drop web shells
incidents.summary: A pre-authentication heap memory overflow in NetScaler ADC/Gateway's SAML SSO message parser lets an unauthenticated attacker achieve remote code execution on any appliance configured as an AAA virtual server or a Gateway running SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN, or RDP Proxy. Citrix patched it the same day it was disclosed, Jun 30, but WatchTowr reproduced pre-auth RCE and released working PoC Aug 14; Previdian then observed live exploitation dropping web shells and running discovery commands. CISA added it to KEV Aug 26 with an Aug 29 federal deadline. Durable catch: web shells named x.php or z.php in a NetScaler-reachable path — even on an already-patched appliance, since exploitation predates some organizations' patch timelines.
facts: CVSS 8.8 · PRE-AUTH RCE VIA SAML PARSER OVERFLOW
WEB SHELLS x.php / z.php OBSERVED IN THE WILD
PREVIDIAN: 36 EXPLOIT ATTEMPTS FROM 12 UNIQUE IPs OVER 12 DAYS (IPs NOT PUBLICLY NAMED)
incidents.action: Patch to NetScaler 14.1-72.61, 13.1-63.18, or 13.1-37.272 immediately if not already applied; treat any patched appliance that was internet-facing between Jun 30 and patch date as potentially compromised and search for x.php/z.php web shells; review AAA/Gateway access logs for discovery commands (id, echo) run through the web interface.

iocs.context: NetScaler ADC/Gateway SAML SSO pre-auth heap overflow RCE
Fixed releases, patched Jun 30 2026 same-day as disclosure
Web shell filenames dropped post-exploitation

incidents.title: ServiceNow patches three CVSS 10.0 flaws in the Now/AI Platform enabling unauthenticated RCE and SQL injection
incidents.summary: ServiceNow disclosed four vulnerabilities Aug 27: CVE-2026-18885, a code-injection flaw in the GraphQL Composite Data API letting an unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code and read or modify instance data; CVE-2026-18886, an access-control gap in the system-configuration image-upload processor enabling unauthenticated privilege escalation; CVE-2026-74820, an unauthenticated SQL-injection flaw against the instance database; and CVE-2026-6876, a high-severity Now Platform sandbox escape. ServiceNow pushed the fix to hosted instances automatically but self-hosted customers must patch manually. Durable catch: unauthenticated GraphQL Composite Data API calls or image-upload processor requests against a ServiceNow instance — normal usage never reaches these endpoints without authentication.
facts: 3 OF 4 FLAWS RATED CVSS 10.0
HOSTED INSTANCES AUTO-PATCHED · SELF-HOSTED MUST ACT
incidents.action: Apply KB3152242 immediately on any self-hosted ServiceNow instance (Xanadu Patch 11 HF 7a, Yokohama Patch 12 HF 3b, Zurich Patch 7b HF 3, or later); confirm hosted-instance auto-patch was applied; review GraphQL Composite Data API and image-upload processor logs for unauthenticated calls since disclosure.

iocs.context: ServiceNow AI Platform/Now Platform unauth code injection, access-control bypass, SQLi, sandbox escape

iocs.value: KB3152242 — Xanadu Patch 11 HF 7a / Yokohama Patch 12 HF 3b / Zurich Patch 7b HF 3
iocs.context: Fixed releases for self-hosted customers

iocs.value: Unauthenticated requests to GraphQL Composite Data API or system-configuration image-upload processor
iocs.context: Exploitation pattern for CVE-2026-18885/18886

incidents.title: CVE-2026-18431 — Avada theme's 6-step exploit chain lets unauthenticated attackers run PHP on 1M+ WordPress sites
incidents.summary: Argus found and reproduced a chain of six authorization, input-validation, trust-boundary, and file-handling weaknesses in the Avada theme and Fusion Builder plugin that, executed in a specific order, let an unauthenticated attacker achieve arbitrary PHP code execution with zero clicks. Argus reported it Aug 5; ThemeFusion shipped Avada 7.16.1 and Fusion Builder 3.16.1 on Aug 27, one day before public technical detail. Avada powers over a million WordPress sites. Durable catch: the exploit requires all six weaknesses to fire in sequence — any WAF rule or monitoring that catches step one (the authorization bypass) prevents the entire chain regardless of patch status.
facts: CVSS 9.8 · 6-STEP ZERO-CLICK CHAIN
1M+ SITES RUN AVADA/FUSION BUILDER
incidents.action: Update Avada to 7.16.1 and Fusion Builder to 3.16.1 or later immediately; scan for unexpected admin accounts, unfamiliar PHP files, or redirect injections added since Aug 5 (the report date) as a sign of pre-patch exploitation; treat any site that delayed patching past Aug 27 as potentially compromised.

iocs.context: Avada theme/Fusion Builder 6-step chain — unauth zero-click PHP code execution
Fixed releases for versions through Avada 7.16 / Fusion Builder 3.16

incidents.title: Boston Scientific cyberattack disrupts global order processing and shipping
incidents.summary: Medical device giant Boston Scientific identified a cyberattack Aug 25 that has prevented access to certain operating systems and business applications, disrupting its ability to process and ship customer orders worldwide; employees at its Cork, Ireland manufacturing site were sent home unable to work. The company engaged a third-party incident-response firm and filed an SEC Form 8-K; its investigation to date shows no impact to implantable cardiac rhythm management device function or data transmission. No attacker has publicly claimed responsibility as of this writing. Durable catch: a global manufacturer with a medical-device product line going dark on order/shipping systems without a claimed ransomware group is itself a signal worth tracking — the absence of a leak-site listing doesn't mean the incident is contained.
facts: GLOBAL ORDER/SHIPPING DISRUPTION · CORK, IRELAND PLANT IDLED
NO CRM DEVICE IMPACT CONFIRMED TO DATE
incidents.action: Healthcare-supply-chain partners of Boston Scientific should confirm alternate ordering/shipping channels given the disruption; medical device manufacturers generally should verify segmentation between business/ERP systems and any systems touching device telemetry or manufacturing control, since order-processing outages at this scale often originate from a compromise that started elsewhere in the network.

iocs.value: Loss of access to order-processing and shipping business applications across a multinational manufacturing environment
iocs.context: Reported operational impact pattern

incidents.title: Manchester Airports Group breach exposes 8.7 million customers, hackers demand ransom, MAG refuses
incidents.summary: Manchester Airports Group disclosed that attackers accessed customer data tied to car park, lounge, and Fast Track bookings plus airport Wi-Fi registrations across Manchester, London Stansted, and East Midlands airports — email addresses, phone numbers, postcodes, and vehicle registrations for roughly 8.7 million customers. Payment data was not compromised and flight operations/aviation security were unaffected. Per the BBC, the attackers demanded a ransom, which MAG refused to pay; the company says initial access likely predated discovery by a few days. MAG has told authorities it knows the identity of the group responsible but has not named it publicly, and no extortion group has claimed the attack on a leak site as of this writing. Durable catch: the exposed data (email + phone + postcode + vehicle plate) is a purpose-built phishing/impersonation kit even without payment data — affected customers should expect targeted follow-on social engineering, not just spam.
facts: 8.7M CUSTOMERS AFFECTED · 3 UK AIRPORTS
RANSOM DEMANDED AND REFUSED · PAYMENT DATA NOT TOUCHED
incidents.action: Affected MAG customers should treat any unsolicited contact referencing car park, lounge, Fast Track, or Wi-Fi bookings as a probable phishing attempt using this leaked data, and enable extra verification for account or payment changes; organizations holding similar loyalty/Wi-Fi registration datasets should review whether that data is as tightly access-controlled as payment data.

iocs.value: Unauthorized access to car park, lounge, Fast Track, and Wi-Fi registration databases across Manchester/Stansted/East Midlands airports
iocs.context: Scope of the confirmed breach

incidents.title: Qilin ransomware claims ATF hack; DOJ designates it a 'major incident'
incidents.summary: The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives confirmed a cyberattack Aug 26 after the Qilin ransomware gang publicly claimed responsibility. The affected system operated standalone from ATF's main network but held information tied to active investigations; ATF cut access immediately and began forensic response. Senior DOJ officials designated the event a 'major incident' under federal guidelines, escalating departmental involvement. ATF has not disclosed how the intrusion occurred or whether data was exfiltrated. Notably, Qilin listed ATF alongside five other victims without posting timestamps, data-size estimates, or sample files — a contrast to how it substantiated claims against other listed victims the same week, which leaves the claim's scope unverified even as ATF treats it as real. Durable catch: Qilin's double-extortion model means a leak-site listing with actual proof files — not a ransom payment or the listing itself — is the next milestone to watch for confirmation of what data was actually taken from an isolated investigative system.
facts: STANDALONE SYSTEM HOLDING INVESTIGATION DATA
DOJ 'MAJOR INCIDENT' DESIGNATION
QILIN POSTED NO PROOF FILES FOR THIS LISTING, UNLIKE OTHER VICTIMS
incidents.action: Federal and law-enforcement-adjacent entities running standalone/air-gapped investigative systems should verify those systems are genuinely isolated (no shared credentials, no forgotten network bridges) since this incident shows even segmented case-management systems remain a ransomware target; monitor Qilin's leak site for confirmation of exfiltrated ATF data.

iocs.context: Group publicly claiming the ATF compromise

incidents.title: Two root RCE chains disclosed in Unitree G1 EDU humanoid robot — one exploitable over Bluetooth
incidents.summary: Researcher Olivier Laflamme disclosed two independent root remote-code-execution chains in the Unitree G1 EDU humanoid robot. CVE-2026-76639 (CVSS 8.8) abuses a path-traversal flaw in the G1's chat_go AI service's knowledge-base upload workflow to write a file into bashrunner's whitelist directory, which executes by shell rules that ignore file extensions — reaching root over the network. CVE-2026-76640 ('UniBLEed') reaches root starting from Bluetooth Low Energy proximity alone, no authentication required. Unitree patched the cloud account-to-robot ownership check in July 2026 during coordinated disclosure, but no confirmed firmware release fixing either RCE chain has been publicly verified as of Aug 27. Durable catch: any BLE-proximate device pairing attempt against a G1 EDU outside a known maintenance session — UniBLEed requires nothing but physical/radio proximity to begin.
facts: CVSS 8.8 · TWO INDEPENDENT ROOT RCE CHAINS
ONE REACHABLE VIA BLUETOOTH PROXIMITY ALONE, NO AUTH
incidents.action: Restrict network-adjacent access to G1 EDU units and disable BLE pairing when not actively provisioning a robot; monitor for firmware guidance from Unitree since no confirmed fixed release exists yet; until a fix ships, treat G1 EDU units as untrusted network/BLE endpoints and segment them accordingly.

iocs.context: Unitree G1 EDU root RCE via chat_go/bashrunner path traversal (network-adjacent) and BLE proximity ('UniBLEed')

iocs.value: Unexpected BLE pairing attempts or chat_go knowledge-base upload requests against a G1 EDU unit
iocs.context: Precursor to exploitation for CVE-2026-76639/76640

incidents.title: GPUThor Rowhammer attack defeats ECC on NVIDIA RTX A6000, achieves host root shell
incidents.summary: University of Toronto researchers disclosed GPUThor, the first Rowhammer-class attack to break through NVIDIA's ECC protections on workstation GPUs. On an ECC-enabled RTX A6000, the attack forces a GPU reset every 2 hours (killing running jobs and eventually flagging the card RMA-ready) and, by corrupting GPU page tables, lets an unprivileged GPU program escalate to a root shell on the host CPU in under two minutes — the first such takeover of an ECC-protected GPU. The researchers disclosed to NVIDIA in April 2026 and held the work under embargo until NVIDIA published mitigation guidance Aug 25; no CVE has been assigned and no in-the-wild exploitation is known. Durable catch: ECC alone is no longer sufficient GPU-sharing isolation — any environment running untrusted or multi-tenant GPU workloads on affected hardware needs an additional control, not just ECC-enabled status, before treating cross-tenant isolation as solid.
facts: FIRST ROWHAMMER TO DEFEAT NVIDIA ECC
ROOT SHELL ON HOST CPU IN UNDER 2 MINUTES
incidents.action: Do not treat ECC as sufficient isolation for cross-tenant or untrusted GPU workloads on affected NVIDIA hardware; limit untrusted code on shared GPU infrastructure, avoid cross-tenant GPU sharing where possible, and monitor ECC error rates and unexpected GPU resets as an early-warning signal; watch for NVIDIA's follow-up guidance as full research artifacts are not public until Nov 15, 2026.

iocs.context: Defeats NVIDIA ECC on RTX A6000, escalates to host root via GPU page-table corruption

iocs.value: Elevated ECC error counts or unexplained GPU resets (~every 2 hours) on shared/multi-tenant GPU infrastructure
iocs.context: Operational symptom of an active GPUThor attack

incidents.title: ReliaQuest employee tricked into approving spoofed MFA push; ShinyHunters claims deeper breach, ReliaQuest disputes it
incidents.summary: On Aug 22, an attacker registered a domain spoofing ReliaQuest's infrastructure and used vishing (posing as named ReliaQuest security-team members) to trick an employee into approving an MFA push on a spoofed Okta login page, gaining view-only access to that one employee's identity dashboard. Device-trust controls blocked further attempts to reach applications through the dashboard; ReliaQuest says no other identities, business applications, or customer data were touched and no persistence was established. A listing naming ReliaQuest appeared on a ShinyHunters-linked leak site Aug 23 claiming a deeper compromise, which ReliaQuest disputes — no customer notifications or regulatory filings have followed. ReliaQuest's own writeup describes a lookalike domain and a fake SSO page fronted by a CDN but does not name the domain itself, so no domain/IP indicator is publicly available for this specific attack. Durable catch: MFA-push approval on a spoofed login domain is still the core failure mode here — number-matching or phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) would have stopped this regardless of how convincing the vishing pretext was.
facts: SPOOFED OKTA LOGIN + VISHING PRETEXT
VIEW-ONLY, SINGLE-IDENTITY ACCESS · NO PERSISTENCE PER VENDOR
incidents.action: Move privileged and identity-platform accounts to phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) rather than push-based approval; train staff to verify security-team callers through an out-of-band channel before approving any authentication prompt; treat leak-site claims that a vendor disputes as unconfirmed until independent evidence (customer notification, regulatory filing) appears.

iocs.context: Claim of deeper compromise disputed by ReliaQuest

iocs.value: Lookalike domain fronted by a CDN, hosting a cloned Okta SSO page (domain not publicly named by ReliaQuest)
iocs.context: Phishing infrastructure used in the social-engineering attempt — vendor withheld the specific domain

incidents.title: Two Australians charged over TeamPCP's Trivy/Checkmarx KICS/LiteLLM supply-chain compromises
incidents.summary: The Australian Federal Police charged Louis Michael Gaebler, 23, and Ruben Ian Thomson, 21, with 14 combined offences over their alleged role in TeamPCP, the group behind the March 2026 compromise of the open-source scanners Trivy and Checkmarx KICS and the LiteLLM AI gateway. TeamPCP stole publishing credentials from each trusted project and pushed poisoned releases through official channels (GitHub Actions, Docker Hub, npm, PyPI, OpenVSX) — credentials taken from the Trivy compromise were reused against Checkmarx KICS days later. The campaign potentially compromised 1,000+ organizations, stole 500,000+ credentials, and exfiltrated at least 300GB of data; 16 confirmed victims were named on a leak site by late March. Durable catch: repos named tpcp-docs or docs-tpcp anywhere in your environment are TeamPCP-created artifacts from this specific worm, not legitimate documentation repos — their presence means the credential-theft stage already ran.
facts: 14 COMBINED CHARGES · 2 DEFENDANTS, AGES 21 AND 23
1,000+ ORGS POTENTIALLY COMPROMISED · 500K+ CREDENTIALS STOLEN
incidents.action: If you use Trivy, Checkmarx KICS, or LiteLLM, confirm you're on a version published after the March 2026 compromise window and rotate any credentials that were present on build/CI systems that pulled poisoned releases; search your environment for repos named tpcp-docs or docs-tpcp as a sign the worm already ran; review publishing-credential hygiene for any open-source tooling your CI pipeline trusts.

iocs.value: Trivy / Checkmarx KICS / LiteLLM (poisoned releases, March 2026)
iocs.context: Trusted open-source projects compromised via stolen publishing credentials
Repository names created by the TeamPCP worm as it propagated

incidents.title: AnonyMousKIT — AI voice-calling phishing-as-a-service bypasses Apple Activation Lock on stolen devices
incidents.summary: SOCRadar detailed AnonyMousKIT, a phishing-as-a-service platform connected to 506 domains and resold through 168 storefront brands, built to steal Apple IDs, passcodes, and live 2FA codes to unlock stolen iPhones. Operators feed in a stolen device's details and the victim's contact information; the platform then runs a multi-channel social-engineering campaign — phishing email, SMS, WhatsApp, and AI voice agents posing as Apple Support investigating an 'impounded stolen phone' — at roughly $0.10 per call, with 90% of observed calls targeting Brazil. Researchers recovered 200 call records across five distinct AI-voice personas between Aug 2025 and May 2026. Durable catch: any inbound call claiming to be Apple Support regarding a 'stolen device investigation' and requesting a passcode or 2FA code is definitionally AnonyMousKIT's pretext — Apple never solicits this information by phone.
facts: 506 DOMAINS · 168 RESELLER STOREFRONTS
AI VOICE AGENTS · 90% OF CALLS TARGET BRAZIL
incidents.action: Warn users of stolen or lost Apple devices that Apple Support will never call to request a passcode, 2FA code, or Apple ID credentials to 'release' a device; treat any such inbound call as AnonyMousKIT-style fraud and hang up, then contact Apple directly through official channels; block the listed domains and flag the listed sender addresses at the mail gateway; device-recovery/insurance programs should brief customers on this specific pretext.

iocs.context: PhaaS platform targeting Apple credentials/Activation Lock bypass across 506 domains, 168 storefronts

incidents.title: 24 npm packages abuse unpkg mirror infrastructure to host fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA / ClickFix phishing pages
incidents.summary: OX Security found 24 npm packages, published between Aug 4-24, that don't infect installers directly — instead each carries a single HTML file imitating a Cloudflare verification screen, hosted for free via unpkg.com's mirror URLs so the phishing page inherits a trusted domain's reputation. Visitors following a mirrored package link land on the fake CAPTCHA, which redirects to attacker infrastructure for credential harvesting or ClickFix-style clipboard-hijack instructions; the operators initially used a typosquat domain (login[.]microsofte[.]live) before switching to a KeyVal dead-drop resolver after the typosquat got blocklisted. Each package drew only 50-300 weekly downloads before removal. Durable catch: any unpkg.com URL path resolving to one of these 24 package names, or a redirect chain through api[.]keyval[.]org, is this specific campaign regardless of which npm package a victim thinks they clicked into.
facts: 24 PACKAGES · AUG 4-24 PUBLISH WINDOW
unpkg.com MIRROR ABUSE FOR PHISHING-PAGE HOSTING
incidents.action: Block or alert on outbound traffic to api.keyval[.]org and login.microsofte[.]live; treat unpkg.com URLs referencing any of the 24 named packages as malicious; educate developers that a Cloudflare CAPTCHA appearing inside an npm mirror URL is inherently suspicious since mirrors don't legitimately serve interactive verification pages.

incidents.title: South Korean government startup platform exposes personal data after encryption key shipped inside its own API
incidents.summary: Modu-ui Changup, South Korea's Ministry of SMEs and Startups-run platform for a nationwide startup audition program, suffered a breach that exposed participants' names, emails, and startup ideas after investigators found the database's encryption key had been placed inside the API response itself rather than managed separately — rendering the encryption moot for anyone who found the key. Vice Minister Roh acknowledged the failure directly at the disclosure briefing. MSS's response includes minimizing API data exposure, adding cybersecurity-specialist review for new programs, full API access logging, and new encryption tooling. Durable catch: any of your own APIs that return or embed the key material used to encrypt the data they serve have the identical failure mode here — encryption at rest provides zero protection when the key travels with the ciphertext.
facts: ENCRYPTION KEY EMBEDDED DIRECTLY IN THE API RESPONSE
GOV'T-RUN STARTUP AUDITION PLATFORM · PARTICIPANT PII EXPOSED
incidents.action: Audit your own APIs for any response that includes encryption keys, key IDs resolvable to keys, or key-derivation material alongside the encrypted data itself; encryption keys must be managed and served through a separate, access-controlled path (KMS/HSM) never co-located with the ciphertext or its API; add a cybersecurity review step before launching any new API that handles PII, matching MSS's stated remediation.

iocs.value: Encryption key material present in the same API response as the ciphertext it protects
iocs.context: Root-cause key-management failure identified in this breach
